subject: POC success criteria & evaluation plan - Atlas Payments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael@atlaspayments.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2028 10:08:00 -0800
Subject: POC success criteria & evaluation plan - Atlas Payments

Hi Rafael  great conversation this morning. Thanks for walking through Atlas's primary goals for the POC. Below is a concise recap and a proposed set of success criteria, evaluation plan, timelines, and ownership so we can lock the trial scope. Please confirm or propose edits.

Summary of objectives
- Validate Redwood improves routing & intent extraction for moderator flows and payments reconciliation prompts
- Verify latency & throughput targets at expected request sizes (most calls ~350600 tokens)
- Measure unit economics (cost/token) and ensure config stays within budgeted run-rate
- Validate quality against Atlas sample prompts and human evals (fraud detection / reconciliation accuracy)

Proposed success criteria (initial)
- Latency: p95 \u2264 250 ms for responses up to 512 tokens (end-to-end server response time)
- Throughput: sustain 60 req/s with batching during peak windows (burst to 120 req/s acceptable for short windows)
- Cost: average cost/token \u2264 $0.0008 (tokenized input+output)
- Quality: automated test set pass rate >= 90% on correctness heuristics; human eval average >= 4.5/5 on representative sample (5 categories)

Evaluation plan (high level)
- Week 0: Data & access exchange  Atlas provides sample prompts + representative traffic profile and test set (CSV).
- Week 1: Integration & baseline  Redwood deploys POC endpoint, ingest test prompts, run baseline for quality and perf.
- Week 2: Load & tuning  run sustained load windows, enable batching and caching profiles, iterate on configuration.
- Week 3: Final validation & report  run final human eval, cost analysis, and produce summary + recommended production config.

Ownership
- Redwood: Jordan (POC lead, project management), Marissa (infra/sre & perf tuning), Marcus (integration engineer)
- Atlas: Rafael (product lead), Priya (data & test set owner)

Next steps
1) Rafael: confirm success criteria and accept proposed timeline or call out changes by EOD Tuesday.
2) Atlas: share test dataset and sample prompts (CSV).
3) Redwood: circulate evaluation harness docs and expected ingestion format (we'll attach sample_prompts.csv).

Attachments: sample_prompts.csv (sample format for prompts & metadata)

Thanks  looking forward to getting started.

--
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael@atlaspayments.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2028 14:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & evaluation plan - Atlas Payments

Thanks Jordan  appreciate the clear plan. A few adjustments from our side after discussing with the product team:

- Latency: we're comfortable with p95 <= 300 ms for 512 tokens (this gives engineering some headroom).
- Throughput: target sustained 50 req/s (we can spike to 100 briefly during batch jobs).
- Cost: target avg cost/token <= $0.001 (we'll budget accordingly).
- Quality: prefer human eval on 5 categories with pass threshold 85%+; we typically run a blind eval (3 raters) and report average.

We will share Atlas_test_prompts_v1.csv (sanitized) and the traffic profile by EOD tomorrow. Also please confirm whether Redwood will run the initial baseline on our sanitized dataset or do you prefer us to run locally and share results?

Thanks  Rafael
Rafael Mendes
Head of Product, Atlas Payments
rafael@atlaspayments.com | (617) 555-0124

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 13 Feb 2028 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & evaluation plan - Atlas Payments

Great, Rafael  thanks for the adjustments. We can accept the revised targets and will update the plan accordingly. Finalized targets for the POC:

- Latency: p95 <= 300 ms for responses up to 512 tokens (end-to-end)
- Throughput: sustain 50 req/s with ability to spike to 100 for short periods
- Cost: average cost/token <= $0.0015 (we'll report both raw cost/token and effective cost after batching/cache savings)
- Quality: human eval average >= 4.2/5 across 5 categories OR automated pass rate >= 85% on the baseline test heuristics; include a hallucination/regression check (target <= 5% ambiguous responses)

Evaluation & responsibilities
- Redwood will run the initial baseline on the sanitized dataset once we receive it. We'll provide a short guide for running the harness locally if Atlas prefers to run an independent baseline.
- Marissa will own perf tuning and quiet-hours load testing; Marcus will own integration support and pre-prod endpoint config.
- Deliverables: weekly status note (Wednesdays), final report with metrics and recommendation, and exportable artifacts (benchmark logs, human eval spreadsheets).

Proposed timeline
- Wed (week start): Atlas shares dataset + traffic profile
- End of week 1: Redwood baseline report (perf + quality)
- End of week 2: tuning + interim report
- End of week 3: final validation & recommendations
